QF.id: Clubbing, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses_21

question.text: Ms. Ananya, an investment adviser, is reviewing a client's portfolio. The client has brought-forward STCL of Rs.2,50,000 (from FY 2018-19, year 7 of 8 for carry forward in FY 2025-26). The client currently holds equity shares with unrealized LTCG of Rs.5,00,000 and unrealized STCG of Rs.1,00,000. What should Ananya recommend?

answer.text: Do nothing — STCL will automatically set off in future years whenever gains are realized
Realize only the STCG of Rs.1,00,000 to partially absorb the STCL; carry forward the balance
Realize sufficient capital gains (STCG or LTCG) of at least Rs.2,50,000 before FY 2025-26 ends to fully absorb the STCL, as it is in its penultimate year of carry forward
Convert the STCL to LTCL by waiting, as LTCL has unlimited carry forward

explanation.text: The Logic: STCL can be carried forward for a maximum of 8 assessment years and can be set off against any capital gain, whether STCG or LTCG. A loss from FY 2018-19 is in its 7th year of carry forward in FY 2025-26, leaving only one more year, so realising at least Rs.2,50,000 of capital gains now ensures the loss is fully utilised before it expires. The Trap: Doing nothing risks letting the loss lapse, absorbing only Rs.1,00,000 leaves Rs.1,50,000 stranded for one more year, and an STCL does not automatically convert into an LTCL by waiting. Note: Based on NISM Series X-B workbook pp.163 and 165, which set out the STCL set-off rule and the 8-assessment-year carry-forward limit.
